_comment: Edits found by reading the notes rather than by the audit. Every pattern in
tools/voice_audit.py is deliberately narrow, so that a subject sentence using one
of the words does not get flagged - and the price of narrow patterns is that the
same voice gets past them when it is phrased differently. These are the ones that
did: 'the course's reference deck records', 'Unit 5's deck names', 'the Web
Services deck states'. The reader sees no difference between those and the ones
the audit caught, so they are fixed in the same catalogue.
Five are written out in full rather than as prose: the phrase to drop and the
bolded claim beside it are separated by markup, which a prose entry cannot span.
Their `find` is the exact HTML, and the `to` keeps the bold where it was.
Figure captions that say which slides a hand-drawn diagram was built from are
left alone: that is a caption's job, it is where the provenance belongs, and the

edits.why: the market is the content; whose deck records it is not
edits.find: The course's reference deck records the model as a market: the third layer of the cloud service stack is IaaS, provided by Amazon, Windows Azure and Rackspace among others, and the middle layer is PaaS, provided by Google, Salesforce.com and Facebook among others.
edits.to: The model is a market: the third layer of the cloud service stack is IaaS, from Amazon, Windows Azure and Rackspace among others, and the middle layer is PaaS, from Google, Salesforce.com and Facebook among others.

edits.why: the providers are the content, from both sides of the same split; whose list each side came from is not
edits.find: Unit 5's deck names the same set from the service-model side — Amazon EC2 for IaaS, Google App Engine and Windows Azure for PaaS, Gmail and Salesforce for SaaS — and its public-cloud examples add IBM Cloud, Salesforce Heroku, Microsoft Azure and Google App Engine.
edits.to: The same set appears from the service-model side — Amazon EC2 for IaaS, Google App Engine and Windows Azure for PaaS, Gmail and Salesforce for SaaS — and the public-cloud examples add IBM Cloud, Salesforce Heroku, Microsoft Azure and Google App Engine.
